skills.name: concierge
skills.description: Cold-start as the Maestro concierge — the model that reads the state, briefs and dispatches the council through the Council Runtime, verifies every claim, decides within its autonomy, builds, and keeps MAESTRO_STATE.md. Use at the start of any session in the Maestro repo or when a task involves calling the council.

skills.name: council
skills.description: Dispatch the model council (Sol, Astra, Gemini 4 Argon, Opus 5.5, Kimi, Sonnet, Fable) on any project folder through the Council Runtime (`maestroclaw council`) for a read-only study or a write-capable coding round — brief template, seats, verdict contract, matrix, resume after usage windows, and what to verify before a row becomes a decision.

skills.name: discovery-intake
skills.description: Run a software discovery intake with a non-developer — a prospective client, a partner, or someone bringing an app idea — conversationally, a few questions at a time, and write a structured intake record the council can scope, price and plan from. Use when someone says "I have an app idea", books a discovery call, or the composer's Discovery intent fires.

skills.name: harvest
skills.description: Turn the "takeaways" paragraphs of a session-log entry into skill proposals — repeatable procedures only, never facts about the codebase — and land them as a reviewable diff under skills/ with the entry that justified them, so the next agent inherits the procedure instead of rediscovering it.

skills.name: usage-windows
skills.description: What to do when a council or coder seat hits a usage window, quota or payload cap mid-run — recognise it from the seat status, keep working, and resume the same run after the reset with `council resume`.

skills.name: verify-before-close
skills.description: The verify-before-close loop that is Maestro's actual product — how a round, gate or fix pass is closed: an independent verifier from a different model and harness, mechanical hollow-green checks (zero-test suites, swallowed exit codes, byte-identical evidence), per-claim confirmation, and what "closed with evidence" means in a state file.
